title: Statistical Analysis Reporting
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of statistical analysis reporting and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply reporting test statistics in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Statistical Analysis Reporting is part of Probability, Statistical Inference, and Experiments. Start with reporting test statistics and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: A reproducible analysis records its inputs, code, dependency versions, assumptions, outputs and limitations so another person can rerun it.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A reproducible analysis records its inputs, code, dependency versions, assumptions, outputs and limitations so another person can rerun it. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.text: Compare reporting assumptions and limitations using concrete trade-offs, assumptions and maintenance needs; state when each choice is appropriate.

items.title: Avoiding P-Hacking and Selective Reporting

items.title: Reproducible Statistical Results
items.text: For reproducible statistical results, state the statistical question and assumptions first, then describe the estimate or diagnostic in context.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Describe the input files and package versions, then outline how to render the report and verify its output. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.limitations: Treat this as a descriptive calculation; state the sample/design assumptions before making an inferential claim. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For statistical analysis reporting, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a p-value, coefficient or score as a complete conclusion.
common_mistakes.why: Study design, assumptions, effect size and uncertainty shape interpretation.
common_mistakes.fix: State the question, inspect diagnostics and report uncertainty and limitations.

common_mistakes.problem: Using test data during feature selection or tuning.
common_mistakes.why: This leaks information and leads to an overly optimistic evaluation.
common_mistakes.fix: Separate training, validation and final test roles before modeling.

common_mistakes.problem: Reporting a model without comparing it with a baseline.
common_mistakes.why: Complexity does not guarantee useful performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Evaluate an appropriate simple baseline with task-relevant metrics.
